title: Bomba Dance Tutorial with Afro-Puerto Rican Dancer Mar Cruz | If Cities Could Dance

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Mar Cruz teaches through clear narration paired with live musical accompaniment and on-screen text labels. She breaks down specific foundational steps and piquetes, using descriptive movement metaphors.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to Mar Cruz and Bomba dance in Loíza, Puerto Rico
Explanation that the drums follow your movement in Bomba
Explanation of El Batey and Paseo
Introduction to piquetes and Marullo step
Carrera para atrás, Látigo, and La Limpia
Discussion of Seis Corrido and closing tips

cues: Y uno dos tres cuatro cinco seis siete ocho
metaphors: Imagine you're kind of creating waves with your skirt
Think of it as a punctuation, like putting a period at the end of a sentence
Imagine you're clearing bad spirits away from you

steps_taught.name: Marullo
steps_taught.description: A two step where you swing your hips and move your arms creating waves with your skirt.

steps_taught.name: Abanico doble
steps_taught.description: Quick step shuffling feet with back heel pushing forward.

steps_taught.name: El Cierre
steps_taught.description: Punctuation step used to close your dance.

steps_taught.name: La Cuatro
steps_taught.description: Simple version keeping hands on your hips.

steps_taught.name: Carrera para atrás
steps_taught.description: Moving your feet fast just like a football player with hand movements.

steps_taught.name: Látigo
steps_taught.description: Moving your hand like a whip.

what_works: Clear step name overlays on screen

quotes.text: Unlike other dances, where bomba, the drums follow your movement.
El cierre is how you close your dance.
It is traditional to dance without a skirt and even barefoot.

evidence_segments.observation: Dancer walking in a circle holding skirt on a beach setting
Side-by-side comparison showing hip and arm movement for Marullo

extraction.distinctive_method: Structuring the entire tutorial around specific named traditional piquetes (variations) backed by live traditional Bomba percussionists on location.
